ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the regular hexagon $ABCDEF$ is inscribed in the circle $\odot O$. Draw $OM \perp BC$ at point $M$. If the radius of $\odot O$ is 4, what is the length of the apothem $OM$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect OB and OC.\\
Since hexagon ABCDEF is a regular hexagon,\\
it follows that $\angle BOC=60^\circ$, and OB=OC=4,\\
therefore $\triangle OBC$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
hence BC=OB=OC=4,\\
since OM$\perp$BC,\\
it follows that BM=CM=2,\\
in $\triangle OBM$, OM=$\sqrt{OB^{2}-BM^{2}}=\sqrt{4^{2}-2^{2}}=\boxed{2\sqrt{3}}$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: ABCDEF is a regular hexagon on a circle centered at O, and segment OM is drawn from O perpendicular to side BC at M. From the text, use that the circle radius is 4, so OB=OC=4. Connect OB and OC. Since the six vertices of a regular hexagon divide the circle into six equal arcs, the central angle \(\angle BOC=360^\circ/6=60^\circ\). Thus \(\triangle OBC\) has sides OB=OC and included angle 60°, so it is equilateral and BC=4. Because OM is perpendicular from the center to chord/side BC, it bisects BC, giving BM=2. Then apply the Pythagorean theorem in right triangle OBM: \(OM=\sqrt{4^2-2^2}=2\sqrt3\).

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: OM is the apothem from the center O to the side BC of the inscribed regular hexagon. From the text, the circumradius is \(R=4\). In a regular n-gon, the apothem equals \(R\cos(\pi/n)\). Here \(n=6\), so \(OM=4\cos(\pi/6)=4\cdot \frac{\sqrt3}{2}=2\sqrt3\). Equivalently, the radius to vertex B and the apothem OM form a right triangle with half-central angle \(30^\circ\), so OM is the adjacent leg to that angle.

推理：题目给出圆的半径为 R=4。正六边形是正 n 边形且 n=6，正 n 边形的边心距等于外接圆半径乘以 cos(π/n)。所以 OM=R cos(π/6)=4×(√3/2)=2√3。等价地，半径 OB 与边心距 OM 构成直角三角形，半中心角为 30°，OM 是邻边，因此 OM=4cos30°=2√3。
